tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: three weeks of mostly arXiv work on what breaks when LLM agents run as a team, starting with KV-cache memory cost and workflow orchestration. It then split into two tracks: securing agents against malicious peers and data leaks, and tracing which agent caused a failure.
whats_new: LatentLens (Nov 23) reports that a latent agent-to-agent interface often fails to improve accuracy and can degrade it across seven benchmarks, the same day REPA modeled how one agent's local errors cascade into system failure.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent reliability now has concrete failure models (error propagation, malicious feedback during replanning, cross-agent data leaks), so a single end-to-end success rate no longer tells you why your agent team fails.

beats.headline: Running agents as a team hits memory and orchestration limits
beats.summary: Simultaneously resident KV caches become a memory bottleneck, and harnesses that spawn worker agents get an executable orchestration benchmark.

beats.headline: Malicious peers and data leaks become the threat model
beats.summary: Private retrieval and inference, an open-source leak tester, secure aggregation rules, and a replanning step hardened against hostile agent feedback.

beats.headline: Research shifts to blaming the right agent for a failure
beats.summary: Failure attribution traces the decisive error step and responsible agent; TRACE-MAS adds repair for collaboration failures in messages and task dependencies.

beats.headline: Error cascades get a model, and latent interfaces a negative result
beats.summary: REPA links local agent errors to system-level failure; LatentLens finds the latent interface frequently does not help.

beats.headline: Ranking and recommender papers clustered on shared wording
beats.summary: LLM ranking at LinkedIn scale and uncertainty signals for LLM recommenders sit outside the multi-agent theme.

open_questions: Does REPA's error-propagation model hold beyond the three Qwen base models it was evaluated on?
Does LatentLens's degradation result hold on model families other than Qwen3?
Do CoLFA or TRACE-MAS ship tooling that attributes failures in production agent traces, not only benchmark logs?
Does Kaer's protected replanning hold up on benchmarks other than its own Cintra suite?
Do any of these benchmarks release harnesses that teams adopt for their own regression evals?
take_for_builders: Log each agent's messages and intermediate outputs per step in your multi-agent runs, because failure attribution and error-propagation methods like CoLFA and REPA need per-agent traces, not just the final answer.
